review_output: {"summary":"The insert-only COUNT revision is sound for the race it targets. The ledger only grows, outside vendor-cascade deletes. A report row can only be seen by a snapshot taken after the report was created, so that snapshot also sees every event the report counted. Equal count therefore means the same set of events. Every RR reader, ready read and completion publish rechecks the count, so a source change that commits after a check still makes the report unreadable. Example: an insert starts before report_create, the report is claimed, then the insert commits. After that, finish, readMetricReadyReport and readMetricCompletion all reject the report. Lock order matches the earlier version → report order, and the ledger insert takes no metric locks. Remaining gaps: (1) TRUNCATE of FormSubmission skips the row trigger, so no source event is written. (2) The ledger trigger may break, or be skipped during, Vendor/Form cascade deletes. (3) Revision scope is the whole vendor+live, so new registrations repeatedly invalidate reports for already-ended windows (liveness). (4) The ledger COUNT costs O(n) and runs on every page and statement. (5) When a source commit lands between the early revision read and the guard, claim, finish and create raise an error instead of returning 0 or marking the report stale. (6) Tests do not cover exact report-lifecycle interleavings. (7, 8) Grants and legacy-migration dependencies are not supplied. This review is not full Goal acceptance.","findings":[{"area":"source ledger completeness","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015170000_live_metric_registration_source_revision/migration.sql","issue":"TRUNCATE of FormSubmission (directly, or via TRUNCATE ... CASCADE from Live/RegistrationForm) fires no row trigger, so no ledger event is written and the COUNT revision does not change.","evidence":"L27-28: the trigger covers only AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE FOR EACH ROW. There is no TRUNCATE guard on FormSubmission; the no_truncate guard (L37-38) protects only the ledger.","impact":"Interleaving: report R is ready with inputRegistrationRevision=C, then TRUNCATE \"FormSubmission\" commits. The count is still C, so readMetricReadyReport returns R as current even though its verified source rows are gone. The same applies to a running report's completion publish and finish.","recommended_fix":"Add a BEFORE TRUNCATE statement trigger on FormSubmission that raises an exception, matching the existing no-truncate pattern. Alternatively, have it write one event for every Live scope. Record that session_replication_role=replica and DISABLE TRIGGER are privileged bypasses outside the guarantee.","required_test":"Inside a transaction: create a ready report, then TRUNCATE FormSubmission (and TRUNCATE Live CASCADE). Assert the truncate is rejected, or that readMetricReadyReport returns report_not_current.","severity":"medium","confidence":0.8},{"area":"cascade delete / FK interaction","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015170000_live_metric_registration_source_revision/migration.sql","issue":"While a Vendor is being deleted, the AFTER DELETE trigger on FormSubmission can insert ledger rows that reference that Vendor. Depending on cascade order, this either fails the FK or is silently skipped. The trigger never checks that the vendor still exists.","evidence":"L5: the ledger FK points to Vendor ON DELETE CASCADE. L21-23: the trigger inserts using Live.vendorId for each verified OLD row. L32: the immutable trigger only allows deletes once the Vendor is gone. FormSubmission/Form/Live cascade actions are in legacy migrations that were not supplied.","impact":"Interleaving: DELETE Vendor V. The RI cascade deletes V's ledger rows and Live/Form rows in trigger order. If a FormSubmission cascade fires while its Live row is still visible, the trigger inserts a (V, live) event. That row's FK check then finds V deleted, so the whole vendor/GDPR deletion fails. If Live goes first, no event is written, which is harmless only because the scope is disappearing.","recommended_fix":"In the trigger, skip the insert when the Vendor row is not visible (join public.\"Vendor\" in the scope query), or join Live with Vendor. Confirm the legacy FK actions for FormSubmission→RegistrationForm/Live and add a vendor-delete regression test.","required_test":"Seed a vendor with Live, Form, verified FormSubmissions, ledger rows and reports. DELETE Vendor and assert it succeeds, leaves no orphaned ledger rows and raises no FK error.","severity":"medium","confidence":0.45},{"area":"revision scope / liveness","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015170000_live_metric_registration_source_revision/migration.sql","issue":"The revision is scoped to the whole (vendorId, liveId). Any verified submission change, including ones with verifiedAt after a report's ended window or for another version, invalidates every report for that live.","evidence":"L23: events carry only vendorId/liveId. L41: COUNT is taken over the whole scope. Report windows must already have ended (report L72), but new registrations during an active live still change the count.","impact":"Interleaving: claim R at count C, the worker reads its RR snapshot, a new registration T commits (count C+1, verifiedAt=now, outside R's window), and finish marks R stale. Ready reports for closed or replay windows also turn unavailable after every new registration.","recommended_fix":"Store old/new verifiedAt (and formId) in each event and bind reports to a count of events that touch their window, e.g. COUNT where old or new verifiedAt falls in [windowStart, windowEnd). The guard (L34-37) recomputes with a fresh RC statement snapshot and RAISEs. The early stale branches (L99-104, L136-141) only catch differences that were already visible.","impact":"Interleaving for finish: (1) finish reads count C at L131. (2) A verified FormSubmission insert commits (C+1). (3) The L136 check passes against C. (4) The UPDATE to ready fires the guard, which sees C+1 and raises. The finish transaction aborts with an exception, and R stays 'running' until the lease expires, when the next claim marks it stale. Integrity is preserved; this is a liveness and error-handling issue.","recommended_fix":"Recompute both revisions after acquiring the version lock. Wrap the guarded UPDATE in BEGIN ...
